title: Bleeding Control
steps: Put on gloves or use a clean barrier if available.
Apply firm direct pressure with a clean cloth or bandage.
If blood soaks through, add more layers without removing the first.
Elevate the injured area above heart level if possible.
Apply a pressure wrap to hold the dressing in place.
Monitor for shock and keep the person warm.
warnings: Do not use a tourniquet unless trained and bleeding is life-threatening.
seekHelp: Bleeding does not slow after 10 minutes of pressure.
Blood is spurting or pooling rapidly.
Signs of shock: pale skin, confusion, rapid breathing.

title: Minor Burn Care
steps: Remove the source of heat and cool the area with clean, cool water.
Continue cooling for 10-20 minutes if possible.
Remove tight items like rings before swelling starts.
Cover with a clean, non-stick dressing or cloth.
Keep the person hydrated and comfortable.
warnings: Do not apply butter, oils, or toothpaste.
seekHelp: Burn is larger than the person's palm.
Burn is on face, hands, feet, or genitals.
Skin looks white, charred, or leathery.

title: Sprain or Strain
steps: Stop activity and rest the injured area.
Apply a cold pack for 10-15 minutes at a time.
Wrap with an elastic bandage for light compression.
Elevate the limb to reduce swelling.
Check circulation and loosen if numbness occurs.
warnings: Do not wrap so tightly that toes or fingers turn blue.
Avoid heat in the first 24 hours.
seekHelp: Severe pain or inability to bear weight.
